newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Afrexim bank to fund Nigeria-Egypt steel pact.
newsitem.headline: Afrexim bank to fund Nigeria-Egypt steel pact.

text.p: The Cairo-based African Export-Import Bank (AFREXIM) has agreed in principle to finance the purchase of steel and other products to the tune of $14 million from Nigerian and Egyptian plants, a steel official said on Monday.

The secretary general of the African Iron and Steel Association (AISA) Sanusi Mohammed told the News Agency of Nigeria in the Nigerian capital Abuja that the agreement was brokered by the association on liberal terms, but did not spell them out.

The agreement involves the supply of 100,000 tonnes of billets annually and spare parts by the Egyptian steel company to Nigeria's four steel rolling mills at Oshogbo, Delta, Katsina and Jos. Nigeria for its part will sell its super concentrate iron ore from the Itakpe mines in central Nigeria to the Egyptian steel industry.

Nigeria's steel industry, on which billions of dollars have been sunk over the last two decades, is producing at a small fraction of installed capacity because of various factors ranging from poor management to lack of spare parts.
Mohammed said AFREXIM was willing to finance similar agreements between African countries in the steel sector so long as it received the backing of the AISA.
